item.title: Bangladesh energy crisis calls for pragmatism, not political purity
item.description: For more than three decades, the Bangladeshi political left has maintained an unyielding stance on natural resources like gas, coal, and minerals, insisting that state entities must develop them exclusively. Foreign energy companies are viewed with deep suspicion, while production-sharing contracts are routinely condemned as vehicles designed to siphon national wealth to foreign multinationals. item.title: As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers
item.description: A new wave of deadly Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities is fueling bipartisan calls in Washington for US President Donald Trump to use sweeping new sanctions powers against Moscow, with lawmakers arguing that greater economic pressure could strengthen efforts to end the war. As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers.

item.description: Recent disclosures about China’s purported in-orbit servicing operations have intensified a quiet revolution in space, where the mechanics of satellite sustainment are swiftly becoming the frontline of great-power counterspace rivalry. item.description: Volkswagen has spent years trying to build a European battery business strong enough to carry its electric-car ambitions. Its latest deal pulls a Chinese partner deeper into that effort. On September 28, Germany’s Volkswagen and China’s Gotion High-Tech agreed to deepen a partnership that began in 2020. item.description: The death toll from Russia’s jet-powered drone attacks mounted in Ukraine while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that the Kremlin is preparing for a new mobilization at home and a fresh deployment of 10,000 North Korean troops. item.title: Deadly Russian Attacks On Ukraine Hit Medical Center, Science Academy
item.description: Russian forces struck civilian sites on 28 September, setting fire to the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic in Kyiv. An office building in Dnipro and an apartment block in Kharkiv also suffered damage. The attacks caused casualties and disrupted services. A wave of Russian attacks hit civilian sites in several Ukrainian cities on September 28. In Kyiv, fire broke out after strikes on the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic.

item.title: Russian Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War
item.description: European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on September 28 that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's treatment of his German counterpart, Johann Wadephul, after their recent UN meeting demonstrates that Russia is not interested in peace in Ukraine. item.title: General Debate ends with call to turn words into action
item.description: After six days of speeches from the UN General Assembly podium, one word rose above all others: peace. This final edition of The Takeaway distils the messages he said reverberated through the Assembly Hall and looks at where the 193-member body goes from here. item.title: UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban
item.description: “No country is free of racism.” That warning from US youth activist Marley Dias set the tone on Monday as UN Member States reinvigorated global efforts against racism, discrimination and xenophobia with a new declaration. UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban.

item.title: DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure
item.description: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) told the UN General Assembly on Monday that its status as a nuclear-armed State was irreversible, arguing that its military capabilities were necessary to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and maintain peace on the Korean Peninsula. DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure.

item.title: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report
item.description: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday. Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report.

item.title: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
item.description: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withdraw.

item.title: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
item.description: World leaders are meeting in the General Assembly to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all. World leaders take stock of global fight against racism.

item.title: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
item.description: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country. DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access.

item.title: Erdogan playing East and West, winning room to maneuver
item.description: Less than two months after his government hosted the NATO summit. which was framed as proof of Turkey’s pivotal role in transatlantic security. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has proposed full Turkish membership in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, an entity that has been described as being anti-NATO or a “rogue NATO. Erdogan playing East and West, winning room to maneuver.
